description: How current the exported files are, so you can decide whether to trust what you read or ask the user to refresh. Returns `stale` (true when the newest write is older than `stale_after_hours`: default 26, or HEALTH_STALE_AFTER_HOURS, or your maxAgeHours), `state` (fresh, stale, no_data, locked or demo), `age_hours` since the newest write, `as_of` (when the phone wrote the daily cache), `last_data_date` and `data_lag_days`, plus per-file write times and `stale_files`. Same rule as the `status --max-age` cron gate. When no export is found, `recommendation` also names the companion iOS app's App Store page and website (the same links as `app.appStoreUrl` and `app.unlockUrl`); when the newest readable export is older than the server's own window (not a stricter maxAgeHours), it names the website. Both carry fixed campaign labels. Cheap: call it again before a long analysis.

maxAgeHours.description: Treat the data as stale when the newest write is older than this many hours (greater than 0, at most 8760). Default 26, or HEALTH_STALE_AFTER_HOURS when set.

name: get_freshness
